Claim: devx lane PM seat, session `e2eac1a7-8000-5c95-9749-38aec2ace6fc`, branch `claude/issue-11800-checkout-guard-selftest`.

⚠️ **Governed surface** (`.claude/**`): the PR **stays draft**, requests review from `os-zhuang`, and is **never** flipped ready, armed or queued by this seat.

**One refinement to the card's framing, measured on #11738 and worth having before you start.** `guard-main-checkout.sh` reads `.tool_input.file_path` and **parses no shell at all** — unlike its Bash sibling it has no `split_segments()`, so it structurally cannot carry the escaped-quote class that #11738 just fixed. That makes this card's surface **smaller and simpler** than "the missing half of a 121-case matrix" suggests: it is a path-and-worktree decision, not a shell parse. Price it on what the hook actually does.

⚠️ **Sequencing**: PR #11799 (#11514) is open and wires `.claude/hooks/**/*.selftest.sh` discovery into CI, and it is **discovery-based** — so a new self-test you add is picked up with no workflow edit. That is the point of this card: right now `.claude/hooks/` reads as a covered directory while this hook stays unchecked. No file collision (#11799 touches only `.github/workflows/lint.yml`).

⛔ **Do not modify the hook** to make it easier to test. If the hook needs a change to be testable, that is a finding to report, not a rider.

If you are a different session and you see this comment before starting work, this card is taken — pick another.

## ACCEPT — PR #11814 · reviewed against GitHub, not against the report

Reviewer of record: devx seat, `session_01UjM2ia8Av1v5NqfqQEQmC6` (seat #6023). ⚠️ Late review — the report landed 2026-08-24T17:45Z and the previous shift stalled before recording a verdict.

### Checklist result

| criterion | reading |
|---|---|
| PR shape | draft ✓ · base `main` ✓ · first line **`Part of #11800`** (deliberate — see below) |
| scope | 1 file, +320: `.claude/hooks/guard-main-checkout.selftest.sh`, **added**. The hook itself is untouched, as the dispatch required. |
| CI | 29 raw runs → **grouped by name, latest per name: 0 failure, 0 cancelled**. ⚠️ The raw array *does* contain two `cancelled` entries (`No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path`, `Part-of PR must not also close its card`) — both superseded and re-run green seconds later. Counted raw, this PR reads as failing its own governance checks; that is the false red this seat's instrument rule exists to prevent. |
| changeset | `skip-changeset` correct — `.claude/**` publishes nothing. |

### What makes this acceptable rather than merely green

⭐ **The matrix was proven capable of failing before it was trusted to pass.** Eight mutations, one per class, each against a *scratch copy* (`GUARD_MAIN_CHECKOUT_HOOK` / `..._SETTINGS` overrides, real files sha-asserted unchanged under `trap … EXIT INT TERM`), and each mutation proven on disk by anchor count **in both directions plus a sha change** before any result was read — never an editor's exit code. The counts discriminate rather than blanket-fail: M4 → exactly 2 (the escape hatch), M6 → exactly 4 (the jq-less class), M8 → exactly 1 (the wiring case).

⭐ **M8 is the detail that shows the author understood their own instrument**: the wiring assertion is the one class no *hook* mutation can redden, so it got its own control by mutating a scratch `settings.json`. A class with no possible red is not covered, and they found that themselves.

⭐ **Every fixture defaults to a directory in no repo at all** — the input on which this hook allows everything. So a case expecting `block` cannot pass by accident; the verdict can only have come from the payload's path. That is a positive-control design, not an assertion.

⭐ **One prediction was wrong and the run corrected the prediction, not the measurement**: `$ODD/brand/new/f.ts` was expected to fail open like `$ODD/pkg/x.ts` and instead blocks, because the ancestor walk resolves to the repo toplevel where `git` prints a *relative* `.git`. The case was rewritten to match what was measured and the exact rule was added to #11809. This is the behaviour the three-zone dispatch format exists to buy.

### The two defects it found — the real headline

Execution beat inspection: both were invisible from reading the hook.

- **#11810** — `settings.json` routes `NotebookEdit` to this guard, but `NotebookEdit` sends `notebook_path` while the hook reads only `file_path`. Every notebook edit takes the no-path branch and is judged by `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` — a per-session constant — so it is wrong in **both** directions: legitimate worktree notebook edits refused, and from a worktree-rooted session, notebook edits **into the shared primary checkout are allowed**. That is a live hole in the rule CLAUDE.md calls a Prime Directive.
- **#11809** — `case "$gitdir" in */worktrees/*)` is a substring match on a path, not a test for a linked worktree, so a *primary* checkout under `~/worktrees/` is unguarded — and because `git rev-parse --git-dir` prints a relative `.git` at the toplevel but an absolute path from subdirectories, the same checkout gets **opposite verdicts by depth**. The identical idiom sits in `guard-main-checkout-bash.sh`.

Both verified open on GitHub, both `pm:blocked`. ⛔ Correctly **not** fixed here — the dispatch forbade touching the hook.

### The judgment call I checked hardest: pinning a known-wrong verdict

The two holes are pinned in `KNOWN HOLE` sections with the wrong verdicts marked and the issue that must flip them named. **Encoding a defect's current behaviour as a passing case is normally how a gate starts lying about itself**, and this lane's standing rule is that a gate's self-description must be true. It survives here because the sections say plainly that these are holes, name the card that closes each, and are explicitly not written as intended behaviour. ⇒ The matrix's self-description stays true, CI stays green, and each fix becomes a mechanical edit to the matrix — which is the right trade. ⛔ Whoever lands #11809 or #11810 must flip these cases in the same PR.

### Declared narrowing — accepted

`check:doc-formula-expressions` not run locally (needs a full workspace install; the deliverable is one shell file needing only `jq` + `git`, and the diff adds no doc or formula content). CI ran it and is green.

### ⭐ Ruling on `Part of` vs `Fixes` — this card CLOSES when the PR merges

The dev used `Part of` and left the call to the reviewer, which was right. My ruling: **#11800's goal is fully met by this PR** — it asked for the missing case matrix, and the matrix exists, is hermetic, and is picked up by #11799's discovery with no workflow edit. The two defects are *findings of* the matrix, not unfinished parts of it, and each now has its own card carrying its own remedy.

⇒ Close #11800 when PR #11814 merges. ⛔ Not before — and since this is a governed surface, that merge is the maintainer's. Recorded here so the next shift does not read the open card as outstanding work.

### ⛔ Governed surface — terminal handling

`.claude/**`. This seat will not merge, flip ready, queue, or arm. Review recorded here ✓ · stays draft ✓ · review already requested from `os-zhuang` (verified) ✓ · listed under "awaiting a human merge" in the round report ✓.

## Closing — PR #11814 merged; this is the residual half-state the previous review predicted

devx lane PM, session `session_01PfaSTikked61BkcsB5Rn69`, round 13.

The ACCEPT review on this card (2026-08-25T06:33Z) ruled explicitly: *"Close #11800 when PR #11814 merges. ⛔ Not before."* The PR used **`Part of #11800`**, the sanctioned partial-delivery spelling, so GitHub never auto-closed the card and the close is a deliberate act — exactly as that ruling anticipated.

**PR #11814 merged 2026-08-25T11:12:11Z** (`merged_by os-trump`). Verified on `origin/main` by output, not by the PR's field:

```
git show origin/main:.claude/hooks/guard-main-checkout.selftest.sh | wc -l   -> 320
negative control: guard-does-not-exist.selftest.sh                          -> fatal: path does not exist
merge commit                                                                -> da5cf88d5
```

⭐ **Why this card looked dead and was not — worth recording, because the lane hit the same shape twice today.** A `git ls-remote 'claude/issue-11800*'` returns **nothing**, which reads as "the claimed branch was never pushed". It was pushed, merged, and then **deleted on merge**. Branch-absence has at least three causes — never pushed, deleted after merge, or a measurement dispatch that correctly produces no commits — and they are indistinguishable from the remote-ref reading alone. #9165 was the measurement case earlier this round; this is the merged case. ⛔ In this lane, a missing branch is not evidence of a dead dispatch until the card's own claim comment and thread have been read.

Residual `pm:dispatched` stripped in the same act. The two defects the matrix found (#11809, #11810) remain open on their own cards, both `pm:blocked` — ⚠️ whoever lands either **must flip the matching `KNOWN HOLE` case in `guard-main-checkout.selftest.sh` in the same PR**, per the accepted review.
